messages:
Maria S (Support): Heads up — since the rate-limit policy push at 15:00 we've had 6 separate customer escalations reporting 429s and a couple latency complaints. Examples pinned below.
Alex (Customer): Getting consistent 429s when hitting our batch endpoint, happened right after 15:02. Response headers show `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`.
Maria S (Support): Repro steps from Alex: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"inputs": [...]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` run in a loop ~4 rps for ~60s.
Kyle (Oncall): DeployBot shows the new rate-policy config rolled to canary at 20% at 15:00, then bumped to 50% at 15:10. Canary metrics look OK but we see localized spike in 429s from eu-west customers.
DeployBot: Canary rollout event: rate-policy-v3 -> 20% at 15:00, -> 50% at 15:10.
Sara (Eng-Platform): Which parameter changed? I pushed the policy that reduced per-key burst from 400 -> 150 tokens/sec and tightened sustained rate to 60 rps. Intended to reduce cost for small noisy keys.
Nikhil (Eng-SRE): We have telemetry showing queue growth on the inference pool handling EU region. Latency up ~120ms p95 and 429s correlate with queue overflow events.
Alex (Customer): We do have a retry loop in the SDK that backs off aggressively, but the first 429 comes quickly. Logs attached.
Maria S (Support): Several customers are asking for immediate rollback or exemptions. What are the options?
Kyle (Oncall): Short-term: revert the canary to previous policy (v2) only for the affected region or globally. Medium-term: increase burst window for keys flagged as PLG or add an allowlist for high-volume customers.
Sara (Eng-Platform): Can do rollback. Question: did we update the policy ID or just the parameters? If the ID changed we can flip to v2 immediately; if not, we need a config patch.
Nikhil (Eng-SRE): It's parameter-only; rollout uses the same policy ID. We can push a rollback delta to revert burst back to 400 without changing rollout mechanics.
Jess (Finance): A few customers reported billing spikes tied to retries. If we rollback, do we need to issue credits? I can draft a template once we know impact.
Maria S (Support): For communication: I'll send a brief status to impacted customers and offer short-term credits. Hold on message until rollback plan confirmed.
Sara (Eng-Platform): I'll prepare the rollback patch and target EU pool first. Plan: revert burst to 400 and sustained to previous value, then monitor for 15 minutes. If 429s drop, expand rollback to global. Deploy window in ~10m.
Kyle (Oncall): I'll be on monitor. Nikhil, can you add a tight alarm for 429 rate > 1% of traffic and p95 latency > 300ms?
Nikhil (Eng-SRE): Added alerts and a dashboard tile for the canary slice. Also capturing example request IDs for failed calls.
DeployBot: Rollout command queued: `rollback rate-policy-v3 --target eu-west --delta revert-burst` by Sara at 15:20.
Sara (Eng-Platform): Rolling now. Patch applied to eu-west at 15:22.
Kyle (Oncall): Seeing immediate drop in 429s for the eu-west canary slice. Latency normalizing.
Alex (Customer): Confirmed 429s stopped for us ~15:24. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
Jess (Finance): I'll prepare a pro-rated credit for impacted customers and a note about the root cause.
Maria S (Support): Follow-ups: (1) Sara to expand rollback to global after 15:45 if metrics stable; (2) Eng to propose a targeted allowlist for PLG power-users; (3) CS to notify impacted accounts and issue credits. I'll update the escalation ticket with timeline. :thumbsup:
